title: Production processes - 123 school
heading: Production processes
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: What is a production chain?
questions.a: A series of steps in which a raw material is converted into an end product via intermediate products

questions.q: Give a production chain from crude oil to a plastic bag
questions.a: Crude oil → distillation → naphtha → cracking → ethene → polymerisation → polyethylene → plastic bag
questions.e: Use BINAS table 41 for the flow chart of crude oil.

questions.q: What is shown in a block diagram?
questions.a: Blocks for the steps of the process (and the substances) and arrows that show which way the substances go

questions.q: How do you show in a block diagram that a substance is recycled?
questions.a: With an arrow back to an earlier block

questions.q: What is a raw material?
questions.a: A substance from nature with which a production process starts, for example crude oil, air or an ore

questions.q: Why does a factory mix the starting substances in the right mass ratio?
questions.a: Otherwise a starting substance is left over and that is a waste

questions.q: What is an excess?
questions.a: The starting substance of which some is left after the reaction

questions.q: Give the mass ratio hydrogen : oxygen : water for 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O (use BINAS table 33 for the atomic masses)
How many grams of oxygen are needed for 4.0 g of hydrogen?
How many grams of hydrogen are needed to make 90 g of water?
The combustion of carbon is C + O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> with mass ratio 12.0 : 32.0 : 44.0. How many grams of CO<sub>2</sub> are formed from 6.0 g of carbon?
You let 4.0 g of hydrogen react with 40.0 g of oxygen. Which substance is in excess and how many grams are left?
questions.a: Oxygen; 32.0 g is needed, so 8.0 g is left

questions.q: You let 6.0 g of carbon react with 12.0 g of oxygen (C + O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub>, mass ratio 12.0 : 32.0 : 44.0). Which substance is in excess and how many grams are left?
questions.a: Carbon; 12.0 g of oxygen reacts with 4.5 g of carbon, so 1.5 g of carbon is left

questions.q: Methane burns according to CH<sub>4</sub> + 2 O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O. Give the mass ratio methane : oxygen : carbon dioxide : water
How many grams of carbon dioxide are formed in the complete combustion of 32.0 g of methane?
For ammonia, N<sub>2</sub> + 3 H<sub>2</sub> → 2 NH<sub>3</sub> with mass ratio 28.0 : 6.0 : 34.0. How many grams of ammonia are formed from 28.0 g of nitrogen?
From which raw materials does industry make ammonia?
questions.a: Nitrogen (from the air) and hydrogen (for example from natural gas)

questions.q: Why does a factory feed substances that have not reacted back into the process?
questions.a: This wastes less and fewer new raw materials are needed

questions.q: In an ore sample of 200 g there is 140 g of iron oxide. What is the mass percentage of iron oxide?
Wine of 750 mL contains 12 volume percent alcohol. How many mL of alcohol is that?
questions.a: 12% of 750 mL = 90 mL

questions.q: Air contains 21 volume percent oxygen. How many litres of oxygen are in 50 L of air?

For the production of iron, 2 Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3 C → 4 Fe + 3 CO<sub>2</sub>. From 319.2 g of iron oxide, 223.2 g of iron is formed. How many grams of iron are formed from 159.6 g of iron oxide?
What is an intermediate product?
questions.a: A substance that is made in a production chain and then used for a next step
